The first PT_PROF sweep printed nothing because the _prof build's Metal shaders failed to compile at startup, and my sweep command hid that.

What was wrong: my profiling patch for bit 1 ("skip mesh closest-hit") was written into pt_trace.metal inside pt_intersect_scene as `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && ...)`, but that function has no local `params` — it reaches the parameters through the scene struct. So the runtime shader compile rejected the source with `program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`, the program bailed out with "metal init error: shader compile failed" before rendering, and printed no benchmark line.

Why it looked silent rather than failed: my sweep loop ran each binary with `2>/dev/null | tail -1` and echoed only that captured line, so the error went to /dev/null and each `PT_PROF=<n>` line came out with an empty result after it (exit_code was still 0, which is why it did not look like a crash).

How I found and fixed it: I re-ran one invocation directly with stderr shown (#53-#54), which revealed the undeclared-identifier error; I changed the reference to `scene.params->pad` (#55-#56) and re-ran the sweep unchanged (#57-#58), which then produced the cost shares I used all round: gpu_ms_best full 45.35, no shadow walk 44.05, no NEE 43.17, no mesh closest-hit 4.77 (so the BVH closest-hit walk is ~89% of the frame), glass always-reflect 35.76.

How I know: my own history entries #52 (empty sweep), #54 (the stderr text with the exact error line), #55-#56 (the edit), #58 (the populated sweep). Note this is distinct from a later, separate silent-failure bug in this round: the round-4 A/B base in ab_r4 initially printed nothing because a `cp -R` nesting mistake put the headers at ab_r4/include/include, so the base binary ran against round-3 headers and silently failed its shader compile (#70-#78) — same symptom, different cause, and it is why I now always confirm the base prints a benchmark line before trusting an A/B.
